world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Sign language — spoken-word stress inapplicable; JSL literature (Fischer & Gong 2010 etc.) has no word-stress statement

new_statements.quote: 日本手話には、語レベルでのアクセントが存在する。乗松ら（1998：42）は、日本手話の語の音節タイプを表１に示す４つのタイプに分けている。乗松らは、このうち AA タイプおよび AB タイプの語において、手の動きに弱化が見られると報告している。AA タイプは、後ろの動きに弱化が、AB タイプは、前の動きに弱化が多く観察されるというものだが、このアクセントの存在は、手話の韻律形成に大きく関わってくると言えよう。 [表１: A 動きが１つだけの語 /前/ /バス/; AA 同じ動きが2回繰り返される語 /電気/ /方法/; AB 異なる動きが連続する語 /司会/ /部屋/; AA’ 同じ動きが異なる手で繰り返される語 /スケート/]
new_statements.translation: Japanese Sign Language has accent at the word level. Norimatsu et al. (1998: 42) divide the syllable types of JSL words into the four types shown in Table 1. Norimatsu et al. report that in AA-type and AB-type words, weakening of the hand movement is observed: in the AA type the weakening is mostly observed on the second (latter) movement, and in the AB type mostly on the first (former) movement; the existence of this accent can be said to bear heavily on the formation of sign-language prosody. [Table 1: A = words with a single movement, e.g. FRONT, BUS; AA = words in which the same movement is repeated twice, e.g. ELECTRICITY, METHOD; AB = words with two different movements in sequence, e.g. CHAIRPERSON, ROOM; AA' = same movement repeated by the other hand, e.g. SKATE.]
new_statements.citation: Shimotani, Natsuko (下谷奈津子). 2023. M2L2 の手話学習者における発話リズム: 動きと韻律に着目して. 手話学研究 32(2): 23-30. doi:10.7877/jasl.32.2_23
new_statements.locator: pp. 23-24, section 2.1 語の音節構造（動き）, with Table 1 (p. 26)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: FILE + Locator: (J-STAGE open access, 8 pp., text present, no scanned needed). I re-extracted the text independently (extracted text, not the compiler) and the prose passage is there character-for-character at the end of p.23 / top of p.24, sec. 2.1 語の音節構造（動き）: 「日本手話には、語レベルでのアクセントが存在する。乗松ら（1998：42）は、日本手話の語の音節タイプを表１に示す４つのタイプに分けている。乗松らは、このうち AA タイプおよび AB タイプの語において、手の動きに弱化が見られると報告している。AA タイプは、後ろの動きに弱化が、AB タイプは、前の動きに弱化が多く観察されるというものだが、このアクセントの存在は、手話の韻律形成に大きく関わってくると言えよう。」 Table 1 (表１ 日本手話の語の音節構造) is on p.26 exactly as bracketed (A /前/ /バス/; AA /電気/ /方法/; AB /司会/ /部屋/; AA' /スケート/); only the header row (タイプ/語の動き/日本手話の例) is omitted and 'AA 同じ動きが 2 回…' has a space — immaterial. the compiler translati…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Visual-gestural modality: 'word accent' here is a strong-vs-weakened movement asymmetry within disyllabic (two-movement) signs, determined by sign type. Reduplicated-movement signs (AA) keep the first movement full and weaken (shorten/reduce) the second, i.e. initial prominence; signs with two different movements (AB) weaken the first and keep the second full, i.e. final prominence. Monosyllabic (single-movement, type A) signs, the preferred word shape, have no internal contrast.
new_statements.exceptions: Stated as tendencies ('mostly observed'); AA'-type (alternating hands) not characterised; hearing L2 signers and Signed Japanese fail to weaken AA signs (both movements produced with equal timing), which native Deaf signers perceive as a foreign rhythm.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical sign (word) level, sec. 2.1; phrase-level prominence, intonation and rhythm are treated separately in sec. 2.2 as carried mainly by nonmanuals and manual tension/lengthening. The empirical weakening pattern is attributed to Norimatsu et al. 1998 (compound formation study); the framing of it as word-level accent is Shimotani's own.
new_statements.identity_note: Japanese Sign Language (日本手話, japa1238), the natural sign language of Deaf signers in Japan, as distinct from Signed Japanese (日本語対応手話), which the source explicitly contrasts. Visual-gestural modality: 'accent' in the quoted statement is a full-vs-weakened movement asymmetry inside two-movement signs, not acoustic stress; whether this belongs in a word-stress catalog is a policy call for the catalog owner.

sources.note: Sec. 2.1 (pp.23-24): 'JSL has word-level accent'; following Norimatsu et al. 1998:42, JSL signs fall into 4 movement/syllable types (A, AA, AB, AA'); in AA-type signs (same movement repeated) the second movement is weakened, in AB-type signs (two different movements) the first movement is weakened; sec. 2.2 treats prominence/intonation/rhythm as phrase-level prosody carried largely by nonmanuals.
sources.venue: 手話学研究 (Japanese Journal of Sign Language Studies)
